chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: John Kirby's band at the Onyx and the White Rose Bar
summary: Kirby's sextet rehearsed six months before its first job, and musicians drank at the White Rose Bar around the corner.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, when I was in the Yacht Club, he was in the Downbeat. When I was in the Down -- he did go from club to club and the Downbeat later, but Dizzie never at and them were at the Onyx Club, and before Diz was in there John Kirby had a band in there. That was Billy Kyle on piano, Charlie Shavers on trumpet, Buster Bailey on clarinet, O'Neill Spencer on drums. He died years ago.

You know, everybody in that band is dead except Procope -- Russell Procope. He was on that band. That was a good band, very good band, and a lot of people used to go in there to hear them. They had a fantastic little group. Billy Kyle told me in fact that they rehearsed six months before they ever played a job. They rehearsed just -- they played different jobs, and they would get together and rehearse; you know, to make a living they all of them had different places they played, but he said they rehearsed about six months.
They were real tight when they went on a job, the first job.
I heard it was a very good band.

It was a good band. I used to listen to them all the time, and, well, I used to meet at a bar right around the corner there on 6th Avenue, which is the Avenue of the Americas now, was the White Rose Bar, and we all would go in
there to drink, and everybody off the streets, you'd run into them one time or another. And I told you who was the attraction when I went in the Yacht Club. Yeah, there was real gas in there.
But all up and down that street you could hear some of the best things you ever heard in your life, you know.
